title: Queen's Indian Defense: Petrosian Variation
line: A pawn keeps the black bishop out, and White aims to take the center with the king's pawn.

steps.text: The Queen's Indian, and White pushes the pawn on a2 one square. It keeps your bishop out of b4.
Put the bishop on the long diagonal, aimed at e4.
steps.after: White's knight comes out with no pin to fear.

steps.text: Push the pawn in front of your queen two squares, to keep White's pawn off e4.
Take back with the knight. Your bishop's long diagonal stays open.
steps.after: White's queen comes out to guard e4.

steps.text: Trade knights before White's pawn can chase yours.
Bring the other bishop out, to get ready to castle.
steps.after: With the queen guarding it, White pushes the pawn to e4.

steps.text: Go back a few moves. Here White pushed the pawn to e4 before the queen came out: a gambit strong players rarely use. It gives a pawn away.
Take the knight. Then nothing guards the pawn on e4.
Now take the pawn with the bishop.

summary: Black meets the pawn move with a pawn in the center and a knight trade, and watches for a pawn that comes too soon.
